title: Effects of Interaction Range on Fluid Multicriticality: A Computational Study of an Interconverting Lattice Model
authors: Thomas J. Longo, Sergey V. Buldyrev, Frédéric Caupin, Mikhail A. Anisimov
abstract: The range of intermolecular interactions plays a central role in determining the nature of phase behavior and critical phenomena. It is well established through studies of the Ising model that as interaction range increases, Monte Carlo simulations progressively approach meanfield predictions as the effects of critical fluctuations are suppressed. In this work, we investigate how varying interaction range influences fluid multicriticality using an interconverting lattice model that exhibits both Ising-like liquid-gas criticality and symmetric fluid tricriticality (similar to that in the superfluid $^4$He-$^3$He mixture). This minimal model serves as a representative system for exploring the evolution of competing critical points within a generic framework. We analyze the model using both meanfield theory and three-dimensional Monte Carlo simulations while systematically varying the number of interacting neighbors, $Z_n$, from 6 to 388. We find that the system with nearest-neighbor interactions ($Z_n=6$) reveals only two types of multicritical behavior, while for larger interaction ranges, four distinct archetypes emerge. We demonstrate the convergence of the simulation results to those of the meanfield theory as the number of interacting neighbors tends to infinity, and we discuss the results within the framework of crossover critical phenomena.
summary: This paper computationally studies how the range of molecular interactions influences the critical behavior of a fluid system using an interconverting lattice model. By varying the interaction range, the authors demonstrate that the system's critical points evolve, showing a systematic convergence toward mean-field theory predictions. This work provides a detailed framework for understanding the crossover between short-range and long-range critical phenomena in condensed matter systems.
main_problem: The study investigates how varying the range of intermolecular interactions affects the nature of fluid multicriticality.
main_result: The system exhibits a clear convergence of simulation results toward mean-field predictions as the interaction range increases, revealing different critical archetypes depending on the interaction range.
method: The research employs both mean-field theory analysis and extensive three-dimensional Monte Carlo simulations.
model_or_system: The model is an interconverting lattice model (DBC model) designed to exhibit both Ising-like liquid-gas criticality and symmetric fluid tricriticality. The Hamiltonian includes terms for intermolecular interactions and interconversion energy.
key_observables: Phase coexistence, critical exponents, phase diagrams (showing LGCP, $\lambda$-EP, and TCP), and density/composition profiles.
important_parameters: The primary variable is the interaction range, controlled by the number of interacting neighbors ($Z_n$), which is systematically varied from 6 to 388.
main_assumptions: The analysis often focuses on the degenerate case ($	ilde{e} = 	ilde{s} = 0$), and the mean-field theory is known to be exact only in the infinite range limit.
figures_summary: Figures compare phase diagrams and coexistence lines for different $Z_n$ values against mean-field predictions, showing convergence as $Z_n$ increases.
paper_structure: The paper establishes the physical model and the role of interaction range, details the simulation methodology (MC moves, observables), presents results showing the dependence of critical behavior on $Z_n$, and concludes by comparing findings to theoretical limits.
why_interesting: While focused on classical statistical mechanics, the study of critical phenomena and phase transitions in lattice models provides foundational insights into how microscopic interactions dictate macroscopic behavior, which underpins many quantum many-body theories.
